_note: Words a comment, a docstring or a commit message in this repository does not use. One list, three readers: tests/gates/test_no_narration_in_comments.py (Python and shell comments), frontend/scripts/check_no_narration.js (the client and the desktop shell) and scripts/check_commit_message.sh (the message). Each pattern is written in the part of regular-expression syntax Python, JavaScript and PCRE read the same way, is case-insensitive unless it says "case": true, must match its own example and must not match its clean one. One entry per line: the shell reader depends on it.

families.name: date
families.why: A date in a comment dates the comment: it says when something was learned, not why the code is as it is.

families.name: process
families.why: A person named where a role or a reason belongs. It stops being true when somebody else maintains the file, and it never says why the code is right.

families.name: history
families.why: The story of how a rule was arrived at. Keep the rule; the story belongs in the commit that changed it.

entries.example: what stood here read the whole table

families.name: authority
families.why: Another product or a style guide named as the reason for a design. Say the need it meets; the other product's choice is not an argument this repository can check.

entries.example: as the Human Interface Guidelines recommend
entries.clean: a human interface for the guidelines

entries.example: elevation as Material Design has it
the way Jellyfin pages a library

families.name: machine
families.why: A path on one development machine. It means nothing on anybody else's.
